chapter: Rabbit Foot show and show life
title: Pay, sleeping arrangements and unions on the shows
summary: Sleepers were free, meals paid for, salaries began at $25 a week, and union and non-union men were mixed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How was the pay? I'm not trying to butt into your personal affairs and all, but I just wondered, did they furnish lodging? Did you sleep on the train if they had a car there and furnish meals?
You had sleepers. They had sleepers on these train shows. Your sleeping was free, but you ate at the dining car. You paid for what you ate. At that time, salaries were ranging from $25 a week up.
They didn't have any union. None of that was union.
Union wasn't so strong as it is now. In fact, there was a few men belong to union that played with none union men because the unions didn't have any restriction then.
They seemed like they just was getting together. I remember those over there too.
It was all mixed up then, union and none union.
